dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.001, unet_c=32, rationale=iter-3 ONE-KNOB: unet_c 16->32 (per-domain SmallUNet denoiser capacity doubled in BOTH proj+img domains), all else held at iter-1/2; n_iter reset 800->400 (iter-1 value) to respect the <=15min wall now that each step is ~2-3x slower at c=32. HYPOTHESIS (denoiser-capacity-bound): iter-2 doubling n_iter 400->800 lifted val only 0.9501->0.9508 (+0.0007), so the per-scan Adam fit has CONVERGED -- n_iter is saturated and is NOT the lever. The 0.9508 plateau is therefore the c=16 SmallUNet's REPRESENTATIONAL ceiling, not a step-budget undershoot. Doubling unet_c 16->32 gives the per-image denoiser the expressive capacity to recover finer structure on each val scan's own measurements and should lift val above 0.9508. Wall: c=32 ~2-3x s/step; warm 3ep + 4 scenes x 400 steps capped by outer_wall_s=1500 (~<=15min). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).

dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.0003, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-4 ONE-KNOB: per-scan Adam lr 1e-3->3e-4. unet_c RESET 32->16 (back to the 0.9508 baseline; iter-3's c=32 did NOT help -> +capacity is not the lever); n_iter held at 400, all other knobs at iter-1/2 baseline. FAILURE MODE: across iters 1-3 neither optimization budget (n_iter 400->800: SSIM 0.9501->0.9508 PSNR 37.53->38.21, marginal) NOR capacity (unet_c 16->32: SSIM 0.9508->0.9502, PSNR 38.21->36.90, NO gain) moved the 0.9508 plateau. So the lever is NOT optimization budget or model size -- it is the REGULARIZATION / operating-point of the per-image self-supervised fit. HYPOTHESIS (per-scan-overfit-anchor): mirrors the demo_dl n2i sibling -- per-image U-Net N2I has NO early-stop in the per-scan loop, so each single scan can OVERFIT its own (GT-free, angular-subset) measurements; on demo, more steps made it WORSE and the FIX was lowering the per-scan lr to stay near the warm-start init. Dropping lr 1e-3->3e-4 anchors each per-scan Adam fit near the GT-free warm-start initialisation (solver shares cfg['lr'] for both the warm-start pre-pass and the per-scan fit, ddssl_ldct-free solver lines 122 & 239), trading raw fit for regularization and should lift val above 0.9508. Wall: identical step count to iter-1 (unet_c=16, n_iter=400, val_n=4) which ran ~13.5 min; outer_wall_s=1500 caps it <=15 min. grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).

dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-5 ONE-KNOB: shared Adam lr 3e-4->1e-4 (per-scan-fit + warm-start both read cfg['lr'], solver_dual_ddomain_n2i lines 122 & 239). All other knobs held at the iter-4 WINNING baseline (n_iter=400, unet_c=16, pretrain_epochs=3, warm_start=True, val_n=4, grad_clip=1.0). FAILURE MODE / WHAT WE LEARNED: iters 1-3 proved the plateau is NOT optimization budget (n_iter 400->800: 0.9501->0.9508, marginal) and NOT capacity (unet_c 16->32: 0.9508->0.9502, NO gain). iter-4 broke the 0.9508 plateau to 0.9541 (+0.0033) by dropping lr 1e-3->3e-4 -- the per-image self-supervised fit has NO early-stop in the per-scan loop, so each single val scan can OVERFIT its own GT-free angular-subset measurements; lowering lr anchors each per-scan Adam fit near the GT-free warm-start init, trading raw fit for regularization. The REGULARIZATION/anchor lever is the only one that moves this solver. HYPOTHESIS (anchor-still-has-room): the demo_dl N2I sibling's BEST per-scan lr is 1e-4, one notch below iter-4's 3e-4; if the +0.0033 gain at 3e-4 came from anchoring nearer the warm-start init, pushing lr further to 1e-4 anchors even tighter and should lift val above 0.9541 (or, if 3e-4 was already the sweet spot, mildly under-fit and regress -- either way it localizes the optimum and tells iter-6 which side of 3e-4 to probe). EXACTLY ONE knob changes (lr); capacity stays at 16 (iter-3 ruled it out), budget stays at 400 (iters 1-2 ruled it out). Wall: identical step count to iter-4 (unet_c=16, n_iter=400, val_n=4) which ran ~13.5 min; outer_wall_s=1500 caps it <=15 min. grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).

dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=6, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.0003, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-6 ONE-KNOB: warm-start pretrain_epochs 3->6 at the lr=3e-4 WINNER base (lr RESET to iter-4's 3e-4, NOT iter-5's 1e-4; n_iter=400, unet_c=16, val_n=4, grad_clip=1.0 all held). FAILURE MODE / WHAT WE LEARNED: the per-scan lr lever is now LOCALIZED -- lr=3e-4 (iter-4, 0.9541 BEST) is bracketed as the sweet spot: it beats both lr=1e-3 above (iter-1, 0.9501) and lr=1e-4 below (iter-5, 0.9479, which OVER-anchors / under-fits). Optimization budget (n_iter 400->800: 0.9501->0.9508 marginal, iter-2) and capacity (unet_c 16->32: NO gain, iter-3) are both ruled out. The only lever that moves this solver is the REGULARIZATION/anchor: each per-scan Adam fit (no early-stop) is anchored toward the GT-free warm-start init, and lr controls how tightly. HYPOTHESIS (warm-start-anchor-quality): the lr knob is exhausted, so the remaining headroom is a COMPLEMENTARY knob -- the QUALITY of the anchor itself. At only 3 warm-start epochs the amortized N2I pre-pass is under-converged, so the init each per-scan fit anchors to is mediocre; lr=3e-4 keeps the fit close to that mediocre init. Doubling warm-start pretrain_epochs 3->6 gives every per-scan fit a BETTER-converged, more generic starting point (same shared cfg['lr']=3e-4 drives the pre-pass, solver lines 122 & 239), so anchoring near it should lift val above 0.9541. unet_c is NOT touched (iter-3 + campaign-state ruled c16->c32 out as flat). EXACTLY ONE knob changes (pretrain_epochs). Wall: warm-start is +3 epochs x 200 train steps (~150-200s extra on top of iter-4's 616s); per-scene loop unchanged and capped by outer_wall_s=1500 -> <=15 min. grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).

The ONLY remaining lever with a LIVE positive signal is the QUALITY of the warm-start anchor: iter-6 doubled pretrain_epochs 3->6 and lifted val 0.9541->0.9558 (+0.0017), the campaign's freshest gain. HYPOTHESIS (warm-start-anchor-quality-still-climbing): the per-scan Adam fit (no early-stop) is regularized by anchoring toward the GT-free amortized warm-start init; a BETTER-converged init is a better anchor, and iter-6 proved 6 epochs beats 3. If the init has not yet saturated at 6 epochs, pushing the amortized N2I pre-pass to 8 epochs (same shared cfg['lr']=3e-4 drives the pre-pass, solver lines 122 & 239) yields a still-more-generic, better-converged starting point, so each per-scan fit anchored near it should lift val above 0.9558. WALL <=15 min: iter-6 (pretrain=6) ran 792s; warm-start cost is ~58s/epoch (iter-4 pretrain=3 ran 617s -> iter-6 pretrain=6 ran 792s, +3 ep = +175s), so +2 ep ~= +117s -> ~909s ~= 15.2 min, capped by outer_wall_s=1500. This is the LARGEST single-knob warm-start push that respects the <=15 min six-box budget (6->12 would breach it at ~19 min). grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).
